reasoning:
Since both reports repeatedly failed on quoting the "placed" field, I think switching it to plain space-separated words instead of single-quoted form would eliminate that recurring error. I'll commit to this change, updating both the annotator prompt and policy prompt accordingly.

I'm also weighing adding an `arrivals` field, since arrival order is a fact that can't be recovered later and would explain the tie-break contradictions seen in rounds 1 and 2 — it's riskier but principled, so I'll keep it simple: an ordered list of positions, oldest first, with ties broken by y-position at the first step. I note the policy prompt about dropping unmatched table detections across consecutive frames only applies within the current step's view, so that's fine. Next I'm considering what color choice to use.

For the color-priority rule, I try "largest required count first," but round 1 contradicts it — green was picked first even when blue needed more pieces. Round 2 suggests first-named order, round 3 suggests something else entirely, so no single rule seems to fit every round's episodes consistently.

Maybe the first pick isn't about color priority at all but about which cube physically arrives first — if episodes typically open with just one cube present, the first pick is simply whatever color that cube happens to be, provided it's still needed, and after that the rule becomes "finish one color before starting the other." That framing seems to fit all three rounds at once.

I'll drop "largest required count first" as its own rule since round 1 contradicts it, and replace it with this arrival-based approach, deterministic because initial arrivals are ordered by y-position. For the candidate filter, I'm also removing the "first appears during the step" exclusion and setting the bin echo radius to 28.

Looking more carefully at the 30 px conflict across rounds — it could be a release echo rather than a bin echo, so I'll fold that case into a release-echo exclusion instead of the old stability rule, keeping the 28 px threshold. I'll drop the stability test but keep the exclusion for detections whose position tracks the gripper between frames.

Now I need to rewrite the annotator prompt itself: swap the JSON array format for a simpler space-separated plain-word format, with "none" as the empty-state value instead of an empty array.

I should actually use the word "none" as the placeholder instead of brackets, with plain space-separated color words instead of JSON arrays — no brackets, quotes, or commas. So appending means adding a space plus the color, replacing "none" with the first color when applicable; e.g. carried-in "red" becomes "red red".

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: using the scene shown and the memory fields `placed` and `arrivals` as updated at this step. `placed` is space-separated color words (the word none when nothing has been placed); a color's count is the number of times its word appears, and none counts as zero for every color.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last entry of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is empty, take the first color in the goal instruction's order whose count in `placed` is still below its requirement.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Color choice: a color whose count in the updated `placed` meets its requirement is finished and is never picked again, even if cubes of that color remain visible on the table. If the last word of `placed` is a color that is still short, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started). Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table); the order in which the goal names the colors does not matter.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: A candidate is a cube of the needed color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step and at nearly the same place (within about 6 px) in all but at most one of the execution frames of this step; a real cube may be missing from one frame while the arm passes over it (at step #1, with no execution frames, any cube of that color in the scene is a candidate). A detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, that is reported within about 35 px of the bin's center (a detection about 30 px from the bin is a bin echo, not a cube), or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: A candidate is a cube of the working color reported as a table cube (not held) in the scene at this decision step. New cubes genuinely appear on the table during the episode, so a detection that was absent from earlier frames is still a candidate, and one that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. Excluded, at every step including step #1: a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center (bin echo; a cube 30 px or more from the center that stays in place is real); a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper in the frame where the fingers opened (release echo), unless that same detection was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step; and a detection whose position tracks the gripper from frame to frame.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Among several stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin's reported center without overlapping it; when two candidates are within about 5 px of the same distance to the bin, prefer the one with the larger y (farther forward). The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Among several candidates, choose the one that comes first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px): the oracle picks the cube of the working color that has been on the table longest. Only when the candidates cannot be told apart by `arrivals` (none of them matches an entry) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame; a point within about 3 px of that center is correct.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: otherwise choose A pointing at the stable cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not overlapping it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not overlapping the bin.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: otherwise choose A pointing at the first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else the cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not within 28 px of it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not within 28 px of the bin.

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the subgoal rule picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames) list every goal-color cube in the scene, ordered by y as reported (smaller y first). At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) if an execution frame shows a cube held in the gripper, remove the entry nearest the gripper position in the frame where the fingers first closed on it (within about 12 px); (2) drop any entry that has no table detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at this decision step (the last frame); (3) append, at the end, each goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px, unless it is a bin echo (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) or a release echo (a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper at the frame the fingers opened); (4) update each remaining entry to its last-frame position. Order is never changed except by removal and appending. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]

edits.modify_to: The value is the color words separated by single spaces, with no brackets, quotes or commas; at step #1 it is the word none.

edits.modify_from: Example sequence over an episode: [] -> [] -> ["green"] -> ["green"] -> ["green", "green"]. e.g. ["green", "green"]
edits.modify_to: Example sequence over an episode: none -> none -> green -> green -> green green. e.g. blue blue blue green

annotator_prompt.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes currently lying on the table, in the order they first appeared in the episode, oldest first. Goal-color cubes are not all present at the start: new ones appear on the table while the robot works, and the oracle picks, within the color being worked, the one that has been on the table longest. At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene, ordered by y as reported (smaller y first). At each later step: remove the entry of the cube the robot picked up during the step (the entry nearest where the fingers closed on a cube); append, at the end, every goal-color detection on the table in the scene at the decision step that matches no existing entry within about 12 px, except bin echoes (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) and release echoes (a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper when the fingers opened); drop an entry that no longer has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; refresh each remaining entry to its position in the scene at the decision step. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]
